metadata.description: Operating rules distilled from real failures: prove a claim before you make it, coordinate agents without clobbering each other, and write work down so it can be closed.

plugins.name: evidence-discipline
plugins.description: Never report something as absent, closed, safe or healthy until the check has been shown to detect its opposite; and never call a fix done until every copy of the same claim is fixed.

plugins.name: agent-operations
plugins.description: Running more than one agent over one repository: worktrees over branches, disjoint file ownership, never reverting a file that changed under you, what belongs in a plan, and recovering a session too large to resume.

plugins.name: ticket-craft
plugins.description: Where work gets written down and how the ticket is worded, using ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Opinionated on purpose, and packaged alone so nothing else drags it in.

plugins.name: session-relay
plugins.description: One session owns one repository. Work that belongs to another repository becomes an issue filed against it and a signal to the session that owns it; the discussion then happens only in GitHub issue comments, each one naming the session that wrote it.

plugins.name: machines
plugins.description: Declare a communication protocol as a state machine next to the prose that explains it, and check it for well-formedness and prefix collisions against every other declared machine before you trust it. Cycles A, A.1 and B: the schema, the checker and the engine; no installer, no dispatcher.

plugins.name: security-reviewer
plugins.description: An orchestrator agent that runs a multi-agent security review of a codebase and reports the findings.
